safetensors files

Source: R/safetensors.R
zl_safetensors_read.Rd

safetensors is the format PyTorch-trained weights travel in. zl_safetensors_read() returns a file's tensors as R arrays; zl_load_safetensors() fills a store's parameters from one, reading each tensor straight into the store; zl_save_safetensors() writes a store.

Usage

zl_safetensors_read(path, names = NULL)

zl_load_safetensors(p, path, map = NULL)

zl_save_safetensors(p, path, type = c("f32", "f16", "bf16"), metadata = list())

Arguments

path

The file.

names

Tensors to read; NULL for all.

p

A parameter store.

map

NULL, or a named character vector from the file's tensor names (the names) to the store's parameter names (the values). Without one, tensors fill parameters of the same name.

type

The type to write: "f32", "f16" or "bf16".

metadata

A named list of strings, written as the header's __metadata__.

Value

zl_safetensors_read(): a named list of arrays, with the file's metadata as the "metadata" attribute. zl_load_safetensors(): the names of the parameters it filled, invisibly. zl_save_safetensors(): path, invisibly.

Details

Shapes are row-major in the file, so a tensor of shape = c(s1, ..., sk) is an R array of dim = c(sk, ..., s1) holding the same bytes: PyTorch's nn.Linear weight of shape [out, in] is c(in, out), the layout of zl_linear(), with no transposition.

Types: F32, F16 and BF16 values are read as single precision; F64 is rounded to single precision (with a zulm_range_warning if a value overflows); I32 and I64 are read as integers by zl_safetensors_read(). A parameter declared type = "f16" or "bf16" keeps a matching tensor as it is and rounds others to its type. Other types are refused.

The header is checked before any data is read: its length, every tensor's offsets (in range, in order, without overlap, covering the data) and every size against its type and shape. A failure is zulm_file_error.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "lin.weight", c(3, 2))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".safetensors")
zl_save_safetensors(p, path, metadata = list(source = "example"))
str(zl_safetensors_read(path))
#> List of 1
#>  $ lin.weight: num [1:3, 1:2] -0.000154 0.037743 0.033246 0.020397 -0.035935 ...
#>  - attr(*, "metadata")=List of 1
#>   ..$ source: chr "example"
q <- zl_params()
zl_param(q, "w", c(3, 2), init = zl_init_zeros())
zl_load_safetensors(q, path, map = c(lin.weight = "w"))
identical(zl_param_get(q, "w"), zl_param_get(p, "lin.weight"))
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(path)
